newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai Industrial up on acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Industrial up on acquisitions.

text.p: Shares in Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd jumped on Monday following the firm's announcement that it would acquire various automotive, infrastructure, food and commercial interests for HK$2.7 billion.
The stock was up HK$1.05 at HK$22.25 in mid-morning trade after reaching an all-time high at HK$23.30 earlier. The stock listed in May at HK$7.28 per share.
"They have purchased a lot of assets," said Vickers Ballas analyst Elvic Ng.
Given the growth prospects for the projects, he said he was revising his 1997 earnings per share forecast to almost HK$1.00 for 1997 compared with HK$0.67 previously.

Shanghai Industrial said it agreed with state-owned Shanghai Automotive Co Ltd to form an equal joint venture, Shanghai Huizhong Automotive JV, which is principally engaged in the manufacture and sale of automobile components and spare parts.
The company also said it would acquire SI Infrastructure Holdings Ltd, SI Automobile Development Holdings ltd, SI Food Products Holdings Ltd and SI Commerce Holdings Ltd.
SI Infrastructure holds 50.2 percent of Shanghai Yanan Road Elevated Road Development Co Ltd.
"The major one (acquisition) is the auto parts and also the elevated highways," said Ng.
"These companies are profitable, have strong market positions and the outlook is quite good. We expect strong growth for these new acquisitions," he added.
Charles de Trenck, senior analyst at Kerry Securities, said the acquisitions tended to confirm views that Shanghai Industrial was becoming a conglomerate.
"One could say that they (the acquisitons) are massive, very diverse," he said, adding that they should lower the overall price earnings ratio of the company.
Ng said the attractiveness of the projects demonstrated the company's good China connections in Shanghai.
"That really means that Shanghai Industrial is well positioned to capitalise on the growth in the Shanghai area and that is why people are very excited about the acquisitions," he said.
Shanghai Industrial said it will finance the acquisitions with a 162 million new share issue at HK$19.50 per share.
"It is also positive from the perspective of more liquidity, or larger market cap," said de Trenck
